Thought: I need to calculate the molar mass of Ambrox (C16H28O) using the atomic masses of each element:
- Carbon (C): 12.01 g/mol × 16 atoms = 192.16 g/mol
- Hydrogen (H): 1.008 g/mol × 28 atoms = 28.224 g/mol
- Oxygen (O): 16.00 g/mol × 1 atom = 16.00 g/mol

Total molar mass = 192.16 + 28.224 + 16.00 = 236.384 g/mol

Now I need to convert 10 tonnes of Ambrox to moles:
- 10 tonnes = 10,000 kg = 10,000,000 g
- Number of moles = mass (g) ÷ molar mass (g/mol)
- Number of moles = 10,000,000 g ÷ 236.384 g/mol = 42,303.9 mol

Let me double-check this calculation:
10,000,000 ÷ 236.384 = 42,303.9
